articles.title: Ex-Packers DT Kenny Clark is having a night in first game back at Lambeau Field
articles.summary: Micah Parsons was unable to face his former team, the Dallas Cowboys, in Week 6 as the Green Bay Packers pass rusher continues to recover from injury. Howev...
articles.body:
Micah Parsons was unable to face his former team, the Dallas Cowboys , in Week 6 as the Green Bay Packers pass rusher continues to recover from injury . However, the other key part of that blockbuster trade, Kenny Clark, is back playing his first game at Lambeau Field.

With the Dallas Cowboys behind 20-7 in the third quarter, Clark helped himself to a highlight on his return as he recorded a sack on former teammate Jordan Love just outside the Packers' own end zone.

As veteran NFL reporter Ed Werder noted on X, formerly Twitter , it was Clark's first sack of the season. Prior to Week 6, Clark had recorded 12 total tackles in his first five games of the season.

Clark was the Packers' first-round pick in 2016 and spent nine productive years in Green Bay. He recorded 35.0 sacks and 417 total tackles over 140 games for the Packers before being included in the trade that sent Micah Parsons to Lambeau. He continued his consistent production during his first season in Dallas, where he had 36 total tackles and 3.0 sacks.

Despite losing Clark and missing Parsons for the start of the season, the Packers defense is looking quite good thus far. They have picked off Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott multiple times, as they continue their impressive run of interceptions . It will be interesting to see just how much more dangerous that defense will get once Parsons is back and up to speed.

As for Clark and the Cowboys, they still have some work to do in order to become competitive in the NFC.

articles.summary: Dak Prescott passed for 258 yards and a touchdown along with a pair of interceptions during a Week 6 loss to the Green Bay Packers.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys QB Dak Prescott completed 34 of 54 passes for 258 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in a Week 6 loss to the Green Bay Packers . Prescott also ran twice for seven yards.

Why It Matters: Dallas' high-powered offense has sputtered the last two weeks, and Prescott has now gone four straight games with just one touchdown pass. It was also his second straight outing with multiple INTs. As bad as it was, you could argue it should've been worse -- a third interception was wiped away on a dubious roughing-the-passer penalty, and his only TD pass on the night came in the closing minute down 16 points (following another skaky roughing call). A matchup with the sputtering Eagles is on deck. We'll see if Prescott can rebound against a division rival. While he remains a QB1 based on talent, his production has reached a point where you should be looking at your other quarterback's matchups before plugging Prescott in.

articles.title: Struggling Cowboys suffer letdown on offense as their defense shows signs of progress
articles.summary: (AP) — On a night when the Dallas Cowboys’ beleaguered defense finally showed signs of life, their star-studded offense let them down.Dak Prescott threw two...
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. (AP) — On a night when the Dallas Cowboys' beleaguered defense finally showed signs of life, their star-studded offense let them down.

Dak Prescott threw two interceptions in the Cowboys' 23-13 loss to the Green Bay Packers on Sunday night. The Cowboys were scoreless in a first half for the first time since Nov. 7, 2021, when they trailed 16-0 at the half of a 30-16 loss to the Denver Broncos.

The Cowboys trailed 7-0 and faced second-and-8 from Green Bay's 17 when Prescott took a big hit from Zaire Franklin. On the next play, Evan Williams intercepted Prescott's pass that was intended for CeeDee Lamb.

Dallas trailed 10-0 on its next possession and had first-and-15 from Green Bay's 28 when Lamb fell on a route, enabling Packers rookie Brandon Cisse to make his first career interception.

Prescott went 34 of 54 for 258 yards. His only touchdown pass – a 6-yarder to Ryan Flournoy – came in the final minute of the game.

Dallas' problems on offense were particularly disappointing because its defense responded to adversity Sunday after struggling all season. The defense's performance offered at least one reason for hope that the Cowboys can still turn things around, particularly because nobody has stood out in the NFC East so far.

The Cowboys (2-4) entered this game allowing a league-high 6.4 yards per play and searching for answers after an embarrassing 24-16 home loss to the previously winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Dallas' defense held a players-only meeting to discuss how to improve. The Cowboys also brought in veteran defensive assistant Mike Pettine in the days leading up to this game to help out first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker.

Pettine was Green Bay's defensive coordinator from 2018-20. Parker was a defensive quality control coach with the Packers from 2019-20.

Dallas' defense responded, though it got some help when three potential touchdown passes by Green Bay's Jordan Love were dropped — two by Matthew Golden and one from Christian Watson.

Green Bay took the lead for good with a 90-yard touchdown drive on its opening possession, but Dallas' defense stiffened from there and produced a number of big plays.

Dee Winters got the Cowboys' first interception of the season when he made a diving catch in front of Golden late in the first quarter. Winters then got up and weaved between multiple defenders to run over 40 yards for an apparent touchdown, but a replay review determined he was touched by Golden while still on the ground.

Quinnen Williams stopped Pierre Strong Jr. for a 1-yard loss when Green Bay had second-and-goal at the 1 in the second quarter. Malik Hooker then made an open-field tackle after Tucker Kraft caught a pass on third-and-goal, causing the Packers to settle for Trey Smack's 25-yard field goal.

Kenny Clark, who spent his first nine NFL seasons in Green Bay, got his first sack of the season in his return to Lambeau Field.

articles.title: Trump says Washington golf course project to start immediately, despite judge's order
articles.summary: WASHINGTON, Oct 18 - US President Donald Trump said on Monday that his administration would begin renovation work immediately on a historic Washington golf c...
articles.body:
Golfer passes a felled tree at East Potomac Golf Links in Washington

WASHINGTON, Oct 18 - US President Donald Trump said on Monday that his administration would begin renovation work immediately on a historic Washington golf course that a federal judge had ordered could not proceed ‌without prior court notification.

The renovation work, which Trump a day earlier said would start next month, has become ‌the subject of a lawsuit over environmental and historic preservation concerns.

Trump in a Monday morning post on Truth Social blasted the judge as "a crazed lunatic," called ​the court case "ridiculous," and declared that his administration had "an absolute right" to proceed.

"The experts at 'Interior' are allowed to do this First Class renovation 'as of right.' They do not need an approval. Work is scheduled to begin IMMEDIATELY!" he wrote.

It was unclear how the judge would respond.

The renovation is among multiple projects Trump is pursuing to reshape the White House and other Washington landmarks.

US District Judge ‌Ana Reyes ruled earlier this year that ⁠the government must give notice before any substantive construction work on the golf course could proceed, and last week issued an order halting the removal of trees at the site, which she ⁠called "inexcusable."

In a post on Sunday, Trump said that work on the East Potomac Golf Links would begin on November 15 and that the course would reopen in about 15 months.

Earlier this year, he said it would begin in September.

Reyes, later on Sunday, ordered the ​Trump administration ​to explain whether it maintained its position argued last week that ​there is "no final agency action" regarding the course, ‌and that at most, "the President has given preliminary thought" to the renovations.

Responding to the judge's order, Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward wrote in a filing that any redesign of the golf course is not an "agency action."

"Just as a decision to redesign all the art exhibits in a Smithsonian Museum would not be agency action, neither would a decision to redesign a golf course, or to trim trees, replace fences, expand the fairways, or mow the lawn," Woodward wrote.

The DC Preservation League brought ‌a lawsuit in February to halt the administration's takeover of the golf ​course, alleging that it would violate environmental laws and "irreparably destroy a priceless piece ​of American history."

In an October 9 court filing, ​the Trump administration had asked Reyes to dismiss the litigation, saying it was premature because the "proposed ‌project remains at an early and conceptual stage."

The next ​day, however, the government removed ​about 500 trees from the site, saying it would improve safety at the park, restore its original design and was part of a 2019 plan that predates Trump's ambitions for the course. Reyes ordered a halt to ​the removals.

On Friday, the government filed a ‌motion to disqualify Reyes and move the case to another district judge, saying her actions had shown "deep-seated and ​unequivocal antipathy toward the Trump Administration," according to court records.

(Reporting by Julia Harte, AJ Vicens and Susan ​Heavey; Editing by Sergio Non, Edmund Klamann and Lincon Feast)

articles.title: Judge refuses DOJ’s demand to step aside from golf course hearing
articles.summary: A federal judge refused the Justice Department’s (DOJ) demand to step aside from a key hearing on Monday over the future of East Potomac Park, which President Trump wants to renovate into a championship-style golf course. The Trump administration has accused U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes of bias after she yelled at a government attorney last week…
articles.body:
A federal judge refused the Justice Department’s (DOJ) demand to step aside from a key hearing on Monday over the future of East Potomac Park, which President Trump wants to renovate into a championship-style golf course.

The Trump administration has accused U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes of bias after she yelled at a government attorney last week to express disappointment that hundreds of trees were cut down at the park without additional notice.

The DOJ accused her of “violating the basic norms” that a judge be fair and impartial.

“It is easy to weaponize selective quotations to bring a baseless recusal motion. But it is much harder to meet the demanding legal standard against a full record,” Reyes wrote in a 13-page opinion denying the effort late Sunday.

“By any objective measure, the Government fails to meet the standard for recusal,” she continued.

Reyes, an appointee of former President Biden who serves on the federal bench in the nation’s capital, oversees a lawsuit brought by a preservationist group and individual golfers.

They challenge Trump’s desire for a massive renovation at East Potomac Park that would shift it into a championship-style golf course, saying the project is unlawful. The president unveiled a new plan for the site on Sunday.

“The judge on the case is a crazed lunatic whose courthouse tapes will reveal, may be insane?” Trump wrote on Truth Social early Monday.

The lawsuit has been ongoing for months, but tensions reached a new high after the administration informed the judge on a Friday afternoon that hundreds of trees would be cut down that weekend.

The judge has said she’s furious and disappointed with the government for not providing her additional notice before the landscaping, and she has since blocked any additional tree-clearing.

The Justice Department in demanding her recusal took issue with the judge’s heated rhetoric — at one point she asked a government lawyer if they were unable to use a phone or drive a car — as well as her demands that Trump administration witnesses show up on a federal holiday to testify before her.

“The Government created an emergent situation. The Court responded,” Reyes pushed back.

articles.summary: El español ya está el trigésimo noveno en el ránking, la mejor posición de su carrera
articles.body: Eugenio López-Chacarra es el golfista de moda. Con el PGA Tour en las 'fall series' y el LIV 2.0 al borde de no salir adelante o ser un sucedáneo de lo que fue, toda la actividad de la crítica se centra en el DP World Tour. Los analistas comienzan a fabular sobre las posibilidades del golfista español de 26 años, del que se llega a pronosticar que ganará un grande en los tres próximos años. Los números, mientras, hablan por Chacarra. Tras su victoria en India sigue ascendiendo en el ránking mundial. Ya es trigésimo noveno, la mejor clasificación de su historia y, aunque esta semana se fabricará otra oportunidad para continuar la escalada, no le dará todavía para subir el siguiente escalón, el top 30. Inició el año en la posición 124 de la clasificación. Enorme mérito teniendo en cuenta que ha jugado toda su temporada en el DP World Tour y sólo ha jugado un grande. Unicamente el chileno Joaquín Niemann ha tenido un ascenso más meteórico. Además de liderar la Race to Dubai, el español también está al frente de la clasificación que determinará el 22 de agosto de 2027, qué seis jugadores ganan la plaza automáticamente para el enfrentamiento en Adare Manor (Irlanda). Chacarra suma 555,75 puntos, por delante de Adrian Meronk (394,31). Ángel Hidalgo, tercero en Nueva Delhi, es cuarto. Con la presencia en el Masters de Augusta por primera vez asegurada, Eugenio ha viajado al Woo Jeong Hills Country Club, a 100 km al sur de Seúl, donde por ránking será el tercer favorito detrás de la estrella local Si Woo Kim y el neozelandés, ganador del Open Británico, Ryan Fox. El objetivo es claro seguir con la racha de vueltas bajo par que ha elevado a 17 después del DP World India Championship (74 de 107 vueltas este año) y si se alinea todo, sumar otro título.

articles.title: New deep-sea cable factory will 'bolster' Scotland's energy security
articles.body:
The UK's first high voltage direct current (HVDC) subsea cable factory has opened at the Port of Nigg in the Highlands.

The Japanese firm behind the project, Sumitomo, said the cables would help power the UK's 'electricity superhighway' - the network of cables which will run between Scotland and England.

It said the cables will be capable of transporting a much higher volume of useable energy from offshore wind farms than traditional high voltage alternating current cables.

Sumitomo claimed up to 250 direct jobs would be created by the factory's opening, with more than 400 supported through the wider supply chain.

First Minister John Swinney said the £350m facility was strong vote of confidence in Scotland's people, skills and engineering excellence.

"As the first factory of its kind in the UK, it will help unlock our enormous offshore wind potential while bolstering energy security," he said.

Swinney attended the opening alongside the UK government's Scottish Secretary Douglas Alexander.

The Labour MP said: "Scotland is helping to solve one of the biggest challenges in our transition to clean energy, connecting offshore wind to where it's needed most."

Sumitomo said the HVDC cables were important in the transport of "massive amounts of Scottish wind power directly to high-demand areas in the rest of the UK".

The manufacturing plant sits within the Inverness and Cromarty Firth Green Freeport.

This is an area, specially designated by both the Scottish and UK governments, where normal tax and customs rules do not apply in full.

articles.title: Charley Hull y la historia de los tatuajes de la golfista más viral: “Me emborraché en Ibiza”
articles.standfirst: La inglesa cuenta a los lectores de Golfweek algunas de sus intimidades
articles.summary: La inglesa cuenta a los lectores de Golfweek algunas de sus intimidades
articles.body: La golfista Charley Hull es actualmente la octava del ranking mundial y está cuajando una buena temporada en la que ha logrado un triunfo y ha competido muy bien en los Majors, quedándose a las puertas de la victoria en el US Open. La inglesa de 30 años es hoy por hoy la golfista más popular de los principales circuitos y en las últimas temporadas protagonizó algún momento viral encendiéndose cigarrillos en el campo de golf. Hull ha respondido a las preguntas de los seguidores de Golfweek y estos han incidido en varios aspectos de su vida privada que la jugadora no ha rehuido. Los lectores han querido saber si estaría dispuesta a hacerse un tatuaje y cuál sería el motivo para hacérselo. Charley ha revelado que tiene tres tatuajes y ha compartido la historia de cómo sucedió. Esta fue su respuesta: “Tengo tres tatuajes. Tengo uno en el pie. Me emborraché en Ibiza cuando tenía 17 años. Mi amigo James y yo salimos de fiesta. Volvía de la discoteca y pensé que sería una gran idea hacerme un tatuaje en la frente, porque mi mejor amigo James y yo siempre nos decíamos: ‘Agárrate fuerte, agárrate fuerte’. No me dejó hacérmelo en la frente. En vez de eso, me lo hice en el pie y dice ‘Hold tight’ (agárrate fuerte). Él se hizo uno igual en el brazo. Volvimos al hotel, nos despertamos con resaca y le dije a James: ‘¡Joder! ¿Estaba tan borracho anoche? Volví con una bolsa de plástico en el pie’. Me dijo: ‘No, Charlie. Es el vendaje después de hacerte el tatuaje’. Yo le dije: ‘¿Qué? ¿Me hice un tatuaje?’. Me dijo: ‘Sí, estabas intentando hacértelo en la frente y tuvimos que impedírtelo”. “Sí, tengo un tatuaje ahí. Tengo el nombre de mi exmarido en la muñeca, que intenté quitarme. Y Georgia [Hall] y yo tenemos rayos iguales. El mío está en el meñique derecho. Siempre nos hacemos promesas con el meñique. Y ella tiene uno igual”. Por supuesto, el tabaco fue otro tema que trató en las preguntas. ¿Cómo te va con lo de dejar de fumar? “Me va bien bien. Soy bastante obstinada en lo que respecta a las cosas, y sí, me resulta bastante fácil. Lo curioso es que Hull confesó que odiaba el tabaco porque su padre fumaba unos 40 cigarrillos diarios. Sin embargo, algo cambió en su vida: “Hace un par de años estaba estresada, así que me recetaron Xanax. Sentí que me iba a volver adicta, así que lo tiré directamente a la basura, y solo necesitaba algo que me aliviara un poco. Por eso empecé a vapear, y luego sentí que vapeaba demasiado porque lo puedes hacer en cualquier lugar, tanto exterior como interior. Así que por eso empecé a fumar. Pensé que al menos cuando tuviera un cigarrillo podría salir, y no lo haría dentro de ningún sitio, y luego, poco a poco, los dejé, y por eso ahora estoy con las bolsitas de nicotina. Fue algo así como cuando me diagnosticaron TDAH (Trastorno por Déficit de Atención e Hiperactividad), que fue cuando estaba tomando Xanax. Llevo tomando las bolsitas de nicotina alrededor de un año y medio”. En una época en la que la USGA y la Royal & Ancient -órganos reguladores del golf- han implementado la regla de distancia de la bola de golf con el objetivo de que los profesionales pierdan algo de distancia, Hull defiende aquel golf genuino y creativo, siempre anterior a la era Tiger. Esta fue su respuesta cuando le preguntaron por qué le gusta tanto el golf de Severiano Ballesteros: “Me encanta ver a Seve. Me encanta cómo jugaban los hombres antes. Me encanta ver Shell's Wonderful World of Golf [un programa]. Pensaba que el golf era mucho más divertido entonces. Tenías que crear golpes. Tenías que hacer draws altos, hacer fades bajos o hacer draws bajos y hacer fades altos para llegar a ciertas posiciones de bandera. No se trataban de pegarle con fuerza. Jugaban por intuición, no eran como robots. Seve tenía mucho carisma y estilo. El golf para mí hoy en día, especialmente en el juego masculino, es aburrido. Todos le pegan fuerte y recto. Es solo un juego de potencia. Pero sí, me encanta Seve porque tenía estilo”. Como británica que es, le gusta el boxeo y le encantaría presenciar la pelea por tantos años deseada por los aficionados. Evento deportivo al que le gustaría asistir: “Me encantaría tener asientos en primera fila para ver el combate de boxeo entre Tyson Fury y Anthony Joshua en Cardiff (11 de diciembre), pero no puedo ir porque es la boda de Georgia [Hall]”.

articles.title: Tiger Woods: Hero World Challenge tournament host not listed ‌in initial player field
articles.summary: Tiger Woods is not listed ‌in the initial player field for the Hero World Challenge but could still be added as one of the three ​exemption spots; there has been no confirmation of when the 50-year-old American legend might return to competitive golf
articles.body:
The 15-time major champion ‌has not competed in an official event since The Open at Royal Troon in July 2024, where he missed the cut.

A potential return in 2026 appeared possible when Woods discussed the prospect of playing at the Masters.

The 50-year-old accepted ​a five-year suspension of his ⁠driver's licence last month ⁠after reaching a deal with prosecutors in his impaired-driving case.

articles.title: Senators get off to a strong start despite being battered by injuries to key players
articles.summary: After a tumultuous summer that included trading captain Brady Tkachuk, the Ottawa Senators started the season without winger Andre Burakovsky, lost top defen...
articles.body:
After a tumultuous summer that included trading captain Brady Tkachuk , the Ottawa Senators started the season without winger Andre Burakovsky, lost top defenseman Jake Sanderson to injury six shifts into opening night and won't have forward William Eklund for the next two months after he underwent surgery to repair torn tendons in his left ankle.

"I feel like every game we have somebody going down," leading scorer Tim Stützle said.

Ottawa has dressed 24 skaters — only Philadelphia has more — and already piled up more than 40 man-games lost to injury. Yet the Senators have won six of their first nine games to get the post-Tkachuk era off to a strong start.

"It's been a lot," coach Travis Green said. "But it's a pretty focused group, a pretty determined group, and we've never been a team to talk about injuries or let it deter what we're all about."

Forward Shane Pinto pointed to positivity throughout the locker room. There are plenty of good vibes in Canada's capital as a result.

"If we don't have our game for a little bit of a stretch, I think we find it," Pinto said. "It's been pretty consistent. And, obviously, Linus has been pretty good."

Linus Ullmark has been in net for all six victories. He ranks second in the NHL with a 1.33 goals-against average and .945 save percentage among goaltenders with at least four appearances.

The 33-year-old from Sweden has indeed been pretty good. He just doesn't want to talk about it.

"I don't really care about my start of the season," Ullmark said last week after stopping 29 of 30 shots to beat New Jersey . "I think it's good that we guys have won a whole lot of games now starting off the season. It brings a lot of confidence to our game."

Depth has been tested and come through, especially on the blue line, which relies on 21-year-olds Carter Yakemchuk and Hoyt Stanley to play significant minutes in the absences of Sanderson, Artem Zub and Nikolas Matinpalo.

"You've got to have young players that can go into the lineup and play," Green said. "Hoyt Stanley's come a long way from training camp. Probably going into the year, didn't expect him to be ready to play games, but he's been fast-tracked by himself playing well and injuries."

Green also deserves credit. The Senators made the playoffs in each of his first two seasons in charge and are again a contender.

On Monday, he was rewarded with an extension that keeps him under contract through the 2030-31 NHL season.

"When I was in the search to identify our head coach two years ago, it was clear to me that Travis had the qualities to move our team forward," general manager Steve Staios said in a statement announcing the agreements with Green and multiple assistants. "I have watched him implement systems and structures that have reinforced my belief in his coaching abilities. We share the same vision and philosophy and are confident we can continue to build on our team."

Stützle, who began the week tied for 11th in the league with 12 points, said he and his teammates trust the inexperienced players who are entering the lineup. The ability to plug and play is a credit to Green and his staff's game plan and systems.

"There's going to be mistakes out there by every single guy, but I think that we've done a good job kind of bailing each other out and helping each other," Stützle said. "If we are structured, there's not a lot a plays going to the inside. I think it's good for us if we play detailed, and that can happen — mistakes out there — but we kind of cover them up."

Part of making up for Tkachuk's departure included trading for Eklund in a deal with San Jose and acquiring Burakovsky from Chicago. But much of the core, including new captain Thomas Chabot, has been together for quite some time and can draw from recent success.

"I think we built on it last year: just kind of being hard to play against," Pinto said. "This year, we hit the ground running with it. We've just got to keep building on it."

Ullmark praised Staios for accumulating talent since taking over control of hockey operations nearly three years ago, including prospects who have been pressed into duty sooner than expected and made this hot start possible.

"Once they get their chance, they take them," Ullmark said. "It is going to be interesting to see going forward, as well, if we can keep this level up for the whole season."

articles.title: Packers rumors: Adam Schefter suggests Micah Parsons still weeks away from return
articles.summary: At 4-2, the Green Bay Packers are tied with the Chicago Bears for second place in the NFC North. The duo are a game and a half behind the Minnesota Vikings a...
articles.body:
At 4-2, the Green Bay Packers are tied with the Chicago Bears for second place in the NFC North. The duo are a game and a half behind the Minnesota Vikings at 5-0. Riding a three-game winning streak, the Packers will travel to Detroit to take on the Lions in a divisional clash. The Lions are right behind Green Bay at 3-2. They'll also be fresh, coming off a bye week. While the Pack prepares for a pivotal matchup, they received an update on star edge rusher Micah Parsons . Per ESPN's Adam Schefter on the Pat McAfee Show, Parsons is still at least a couple of weeks away from returning. McAfee shared Schefter's report via X, formerly Twitter.

"I was told that Micah Parsons wasn't close to playing against the Dallas Cowboys," Schefter said on the show. "They haven't opened up his practice window yet, and I'm not anticipating that right now."

Schefter went on to state that Parsons likely wouldn't be back until at least early next month. His knee injury has kept him on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list the entire season. While it would have been quite the storyline if Parsons returned this past Sunday against the Dallas Cowboys, his former team, his 21-day practice window still has not opened up. Before the ex-Cowboy can make his return, that window must open up.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

With a pivotal Sunday afternoon tilt against the Lions approaching, it sounds as if Parsons will continue his stint on the PUP. If Schefter's timeline is correct, the earliest the Packers would get Parsons back could be in New England against the Patriots on November 8th. Green Bay's bye is two weeks after that. It feels more likely that the former first-rounder will return against the Los Angeles Rams in a primetime matchup on Thanksgiving Eve. In any case, the sooner the Pack gets Parsons back, the better. Their postseason hopes may depend on it.

articles.title: Colin Cowherd blasts Dallas Cowboys after another loss on Sunday
articles.summary: Colin Cowherd went after the Dallas Cowboys on "The Herd" on Monday.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys had another ugly game on NBC's "Sunday Night Football."

They didn't play well in any phase and lost 23-13 to the Green Bay Packers , dropping to 2-4. Their defense continues to bleed yards and points every week, and quarterback Dak Prescott has been inconsistent.

Prescott has only two touchdown passes in the Cowboys' last two games, but he's also thrown four interceptions in that span.

Colin Cowherd watched the game on Sunday and went after the Cowboys during Monday's edition of "The Herd."

"The longer [Brian Schottenheimer] coaches, the worse it gets," Cowherd said . "Green Bay's missing three top defensive starters. He has extra prep time because they played on Thursday. Five first downs in the first half and no points. What is going on? They are 2-4. In the last two weeks, same amount of points as the Titans."

"This is all Jerry Jones. He didn't follow his own advice. He got a bargain at head coach. He wanted a bargain; that's exactly what he got."

The Cowboys will have to make some adjustments on both sides of the ball if they want to stay in contention for a playoff spot. Those adjustments will have to come quickly because they have another primetime game next Monday against the Philadelphia Eagles.

articles.title: Mosley sweep Bay County golf titles; Denecke, Hourigan win solo titles
articles.summary: Bay County boys and girls golf teams met at the Panama City Country Club for the Bay County Golf Championships.
articles.body:
PANAMA CITY, Fla. — Mosley swept the boys and girls team championships Monday at the Bay County Golf Championships at Panama City Country Club, led by junior Cade Denecke's individual victory on the boys side and a strong team performance from the Lady Dolphins' squad.

Denecke shot a 1-under-par 71 to win the boys individual title, helping Mosley post a team score of 317, 13 strokes ahead of runner-up Bay, which finished at 330.

Bay High freshman Kentley Hourigan claimed the girls individual championship with an 81, while Mosley won the girls team title with a 406. North Bay Haven finished second at 416.

For Denecke, the victory was another milestone in a season built on consistency and confidence. The junior said he focused on executing his game plan rather than thinking about defending his title.

"I didn't really think about winning too much. I just played my game," Denecke said.

He said the course conditions challenged the field but emphasized the importance of staying composed and recovering from mistakes.

"The course is in pretty hard condition today, so I just got to hit varying greens and just make the putts, and that's what I did today," Denecke said.

Denecke said his confidence heading into the championship came from a successful season in which he had won nearly every county match.

"I've always had a lot of confidence, and I think I just carried it in today," he said.

Despite his second county title, Denecke has his sights set on advancing further in the postseason. He said missing out on state qualification by one stroke last year remains a motivating factor as he prepares for districts and regionals.

Mosley's boys team finished with a 317, followed by Bay at 330, Bozeman at 340, North Bay Haven at 341 and Arnold at 354.

On the girls side, Mosley finished 10 strokes ahead of North Bay Haven to secure the team championship. Arnold placed third at 448, followed by Rutherford at 474 and Bozeman at 476.

Hourigan, meanwhile, delivered the top individual round among the girls, crediting her improvement throughout the season to consistent practice and help from her coaches.

"I think my coaches really helped me get better," Hourigan said. "My improvement from the first match to this match was big."

The freshman said lessons and regular practice helped her develop consistency, adding that her game has improved significantly over the past three years.

"I improved a lot and practiced a lot," Hourigan said. "You need to practice to get better."

Hourigan entered Monday's championship with modest expectations after a disappointing performance the previous Thursday. She began playing better as the round progressed and found her rhythm with back-to-back birdies.

Asked when she began to feel comfortable in her round, Hourigan pointed to the eighth hole.

For North Bay Haven sophomore Missy Perdue, last years county champion and this seasons girls runner-up finish was particularly meaningful given the challenge of balancing golf with volleyball throughout the season.

Perdue shot an 85 to finish second individually.

"Through the season, I didn't get to make it to a lot of matches because I play volleyball," Perdue said. "I wasn't able to be out here much to practice, but I just tried my best and did some stuff at home."

Perdue said she took advantage of opportunities to play whenever her schedule allowed.

Although she had hoped to shoot in the high 70s, Perdue said she was satisfied with her effort and remained optimistic about the next stage of the season.

With more time available for golf practice, Perdue expects to be better prepared for districts.

articles.title: Patriots Deliver Bad News on Romeo Doubs After Shoulder Injury
articles.summary: The New England Patriots have placed wide receiver Romeo Doubs on injured reserve after he suffered a shoulder injury in Week 6. The post Patriots Deliver Ba...
articles.body:
The New England Patriots saw the long-awaited return of wide receiver A.J. Brown in Week 6.

Although Brown did not have his finest day as a pro in his first game back after sustaining a high ankle sprain in the season opener back in early September, the team will be hoping that the performances only improve from here on in.

Conversely, the Patriots could be saying goodbye – at least for the moment – to their de facto WR2, Romeo Doubs.

Doubs injured his shoulder on Sunday against the New York Jets on a 42-yard touchdown reception in the first quarter, and did not return for the rest of the game as the Patriots won 26-19.

Per the team's roster moves on Monday at 4pm ET, Doubs will miss at least the next four games after he was placed on injured reserve.

Romeo Doubs Placed on IR With Shoulder Injury

"The Patriots placed WR Romeo Doubs on injured reserve with a shoulder injury and signed DB Elliott Davison to the 53-man roster from the practice squad." Ian Rapoport posted on X.

Doubs had not been having his ideal season prior to the injury in Week 6. The former Green Bay Packer had managed just 261 yards in six games; an auspiciously low number for a highly priced free agent that was operating as the WR1 in Brown's absence for over a month.

The 26-year old has also struggled to get open, and even when he has, drops have been persistent.

How Will Romeo Doubs' Absence Affect the Patriots Offense?

In recent weeks, as the Patriots offense has sparked into life, quarterback Drake Maye had been preferring other targets such as DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III.

Yet even with Doubs under-performing, this is still sad and a loss for a New England team that was already thin in terms of truly high-end receiving talent.

There has not been any official diagnosis of Doubs' injury yet, so there is no timeline or suspected return date for the fifth year pro beyond missing the next four games.

articles.title: Packers signing former first-round pick Mazi Smith to practice squad
articles.summary: The Packers are signing DL Mazi Smith, a 2023 first-round pick of the Cowboys, to the practice squad.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers are expected to sign 2023 first-round pick Mazi Smith, a defensive lineman out of Michigan, to the team's practice squad, according to ESPN's Rob Demovsky . Smith was in Green Bay for a tryout on Monday.

The Dallas Cowboys made Smith the 26th overall pick in the 2023 draft. He spent three seasons in Dallas, playing in 37 regular season games, before the Cowboys traded him to the New York Jets in the Quinnen Williams deal during the 2025 season. He was released by the Jets at final cuts this year and spent the first part of the 2026 season on the practice squad of the Miami Dolphins . After appearing in one game for Miami, Smith was released by the Dolphins on Oct. 13.

in 2024, Smith was a full-time starter for the Cowboys, playing 526 defensive snaps. He produced eight pressures and 20 stops but graded out very poorly against the run and as a pass-rusher, per PFF. Smith has 20 career starts across four NFL seasons.

Listed as 6-3 and 337 pounds, Smith is a traditional nose tackle type. While his pro career hasn't gotten off the ground despite three different stops, the Packers are hoping the pieces can start coming together for Smith in Green Bay.

The Packers need the additional depth along the defensive line. Javon Hargrave, Warren Brinson and Jonathan Ford are all on injured reserve, leaving only four active defensive linemen on the 53-man roster: Devonte Wyatt, Karl Brooks, Chris McClellan and Anthony Campbell. Smith could be a potential elevation candidate in the coming weeks. The Packers are also expecting to return Jordon Riley from the PUP list either this week or the next.

Smith will join rookie David Blay Jr. as the two defensive linemen on the Packers practice squad.

The Packers have a 17-player practice squad as of Monday, so a corresponding roster move will be required before Smith is officially signed.
